findings.title: The open dossier goes stale while the clock moves within a phase: 'Position at 12:03' still shown at 12:37, a place's 'Formations nearby now' wrong in 86 of 240 place-phases
findings.user_impact: A visitor who opens a formation's or place's dossier and plays or scrubs within a phase reads a stale position, time and 'nearby now' list stated as current; the dossier contradicts the map beside it.
findings.expected: An open dossier's rows that state the clock or 'now' (Where, Position at HH:MM, Midpoint at HH:MM, the day-track's dot, Formations nearby now) follow the clock.
findings.observed: setClock repaints the dossier within a phase only when drawerKey changes; the key holds each formation's text phase and hidden state, not its place. C1: Napoleon's headquarters' card painted at 12:03 ('Zuran mound') unchanged at 12:37 when the model has it at 'Stare Vinohrady', 4.8 km on; the full dossier still says 'Position at 12:03'. C2: a standing formation's dossier says 'Position at 04:05' at 04:45. C3: 86 of 240 place-phases end with a 'Formations nearby now' list the model no longer has (under everyone's reading; 0 under Napoleon's headquarters). C4: 49 aggregate-phases keep a midpoint the model has left.
findings.repro: node tools/audit-post8/state/props-bundle2.js <isolated copy root> (python3 build.py && node tools/mk-world-mod.js && node tools/mk-helpers.js first)
findings.cause_hypothesis: drawerKey omits the clock-dependent rows' inputs
findings.remedy: Repaint the open dossier's clock-dependent rows when their values change (e.g. include a rounded clock or the computed place in drawerKey for those rows, or repaint those rows each minute); add a runtime test that opens a dossier and moves the clock within a phase.
findings.risk: repaint cost each minute; focus must be kept
findings.validation: the C1-C4 checks re-run: 0 stale rows

findings.title: A theme chosen while the clock plays does not stop it: the clock runs on and Follow takes the camera from the theme's view within seconds
findings.user_impact: A visitor who picks an analysis theme while Play runs loses the theme's moment and view within seconds; the explanation then describes a different moment from the one shown.
findings.expected: As app.js's own comment says (8827: 'the tour and the themes stop the clock'), choosing a theme stops Play and holds the theme's moment and view.
findings.observed: B4: playing at 05:00, the theme 'plan' put the clock at 04:00 and Play went on (04:10 two seconds later). D2: 1.7 s after the theme was chosen the camera target is 7 units from the theme's authored target, at 3.7 s 63 units, at 7.7 s 76 units; clock 04:28, still playing.
findings.repro: node tools/audit-post8/state/props-bundle.js / props-bundle3.js <isolated copy root> (python3 build.py && node tools/mk-world-mod.js && node tools/mk-helpers.js first)
findings.cause_hypothesis: setChapter never calls stopPlay (the tour and the phase and act buttons do)
findings.remedy: Call stopPlay in setChapter as applyTour does; add a test.

findings.title: A phase change that interrupts the overlays' fade makes the outgoing phase's arrows pop back to 0.9 opacity (stepping through phases quickly flashes each skipped phase's arrows)
findings.user_impact: Arrows of a phase the visitor stepped past flash on screen for about a second: a misleading glimpse of movements not belonging to the moment shown.
findings.expected: An interrupted fade continues from the opacity reached; a skipped phase's never-shown arrows stay hidden.
findings.observed: rebuildOverlays resets ovFadeIn=0, ovFadeOut=1; the outgoing group is drawn at 0.9*ovFadeOut whatever it had reached. At 4x with the dwell off 5 of 9 boundaries pop (the 08:00 phase's 41 materials 0.13 to 0.90 as 08:45 begins); dwell on: 0. Opening: 1 pop when Next is pressed at once. Clock stopped, two phase steps 0.5 s apart: the stepped-through phase's arrows (never visible, 0.00) drawn at 0.90 and fade over 1.09 s.
findings.repro: node tools/audit-post8/state/props-bundle.js / props-bundle3.js <isolated copy root> (python3 build.py && node tools/mk-world-mod.js && node tools/mk-helpers.js first)
findings.remedy: Carry the outgoing group's current opacity into the new fade (start ovFadeOut from the reached value), or skip drawing a group that never became visible.

findings.title: The first Play frame after the page went idle advances 120 ms of play (0.6 clock min at 1/2x, 3.6 at 4x)
findings.user_impact: A small jump of the clock when Play starts from the keyboard; not noticeable at 1/2x.
findings.expected: Play's first frame advances one frame's worth.
findings.observed: loop returns on idle frames before lastFrame=now, so the next active frame's dt is the 120 ms cap: 0.600 clock min at 1/2x (a 60 Hz frame is 0.083), 3.648 at 4x. Reached when Play starts on a keydown before any frame has run.
findings.repro: node tools/audit-post8/state/props-bundle.js <isolated copy root> (python3 build.py && node tools/mk-world-mod.js && node tools/mk-helpers.js first)
findings.cause_hypothesis: lastFrame not updated on idle frames

findings.title: The reading ('Whose eyes?') is cached for the clock's minute at the first instant asked, so it depends on the path: 29 and 38 formation-minutes differ by route
findings.user_impact: Under a headquarters' reading the same moment can show a formation as known or unknown depending on how the visitor got there.
findings.expected: Decision 92: the reading at the clock's minute, the same however the clock got there.
findings.observed: B6: the reading at m+0.9 reached through m+0.1 differs from the same clock sought directly in 29 formation-minutes (Napoleon's HQ) and 38 (Allied); Liechtenstein's cavalry at 08:07:54 'unknown' one way, 'seen' the other.
findings.repro: node tools/audit-post8/state/props-bundle.js <isolated copy root> (python3 build.py && node tools/mk-world-mod.js && node tools/mk-helpers.js first)
findings.cause_hypothesis: cache keyed by minute, filled at first instant
findings.remedy: Compute the reading at the minute's start (floor the clock) when filling the cache.

findings.title: The event jumps' 1.5-minute margin skips a start the clock stands just before (20 of 21 starts from one minute before)
findings.user_impact: Occasional skipped event when stepping events after a pause or a drag.
findings.expected: 'Next event' from just before a start goes to that start.
findings.observed: jumpEvent takes the first start more than 1.5 min ahead; from one minute before, 'next event' skips it for 20 of 21 starts; a pause in a dwell's ease in leaves the clock under 1.25 min before the start.
findings.repro: node tools/audit-post8/state/props-helpers.js <isolated copy root> (python3 build.py && node tools/mk-world-mod.js && node tools/mk-helpers.js first)
findings.cause_hypothesis: margin larger than the dwell's ease
findings.remedy: Use a margin below the smallest step that can leave the clock before a start (or test strictly greater than the current clock).

findings.title: The time rail's drag has no button test and no pointercancel: a lost pointerup (context menu, cancelled touch) would leave hover scrubbing the clock
findings.user_impact: After a right-press on the rail or a cancelled touch, moving the pointer may scrub the clock unexpectedly.
findings.expected: A drag ends on pointerup, pointercancel or lostpointercapture, and moves only with a button held.
findings.observed: pointerdown seeks with any button; pointermove seeks while dragging without reading e.buttons; only a window pointerup clears it; no pointercancel or lostpointercapture handler.
findings.remedy: Handle pointercancel/lostpointercapture and test e.buttons in pointermove.

findings.title: The low tier is decided once at start: a desktop page opened in a small window keeps density 1, no shadows and no near detail when enlarged
findings.user_impact: A desktop visitor who starts in a small window sees a lower-quality picture until reload.
findings.expected: Quality tier follows the window, or the choice is stated.
findings.observed: lowTier evaluated once (window area under 900x700 or a mobile UA); onResize never re-evaluates; groundDetail chosen once.
findings.remedy: Re-evaluate lowTier on a large resize, or document it.
